rationale: F001 is the switch that lets photos and PDFs arrive, F002 is what a parent gets from it, and F084 is the gate that decision 3 puts in front of that switch; the switch and the gate give the family nothing alone. All three are wave A under one open decision and stay on the parents' own agents, and the card names the gate and carries medium risk, so nothing riskier is hidden.
name: Photos and PDFs sent to Happy: received, read, and privacy-gated before the cloud

rationale: Both make Happy's reply arrive as an audio file through the same gateway speech setting; VOX-04 only replaces the voice F004 uses and switches the online fallback voice off. F004 never had a wave and VOX-04 depends on it, both are low risk and add no way to send data out, so the pair ships in C.
name: Spoken replies with a local voice (macOS say first, a neural voice next, cloud speech switched off)

rationale: All five describe one outcome, a web lookup done by the memory-less research helper: WEB-01 is its guardrail, F022 and F025 are the answer rules written into its instructions, and G014 is the acknowledge, notify and cancel convention for its hand-off, which its own record says has no user until F019 exists. F025 and G014 carry wave C only from the 9 Oct grouping (both are prompt-only, ready now, and need nothing later than F019), all five are low risk, and every part stays on the research agent or in gateway config.
name: Research agent: read public web pages, with egress guardrails, cited and fact-checked answers, and background etiquette

rationale: F021 is the Places tool on the research agent and F027 is the only workflow written for it, so a parent gets one outcome: nearby picks with hours, rating, phone and a Maps link. Same wave, same agent, both low risk and read-only, with no reservation or booking.
name: Places lookup and find-a-place answers (open now, rating, hours, phone, Maps link)

rationale: WEB-03 is the allowlist hook without which the browser that F020 adds is all-or-nothing; it has no use alone and in this batch it only denies. Same wave and same research agent, and the card names the hook and carries its medium risk.
name: Research browser for JavaScript pages behind an action firewall hook, plus the summarize reader

rationale: Both give one outcome, a single text when a public site the family follows changes, by two routes: a fetched page compared with a stored hash, and a feed scan with no model in it. Both are wave C and touch no private data; the card must name the feed route separately, because it adds a host-side binary, and it carries that route's medium risk.
name: Page and feed watchers for sites that never email (registration opens, district and town pages, school and library feeds)

rationale: SRC-09 says it gives G012 its real data sources: both add public calendar links to the family calendar so the events show in answers and briefs, and SRC-09 adds a no-model text when a game moves. G012 was 'later' by 9 Oct priority and not for a dependency, both are low risk and read-only, so the pair ships in B.
name: External calendar feeds (district, teams, library) in the family calendar, with change alerts for sports schedules

rationale: Texting 'add oat milk' in F032 is the add tool that F030 builds; F032 adds only one scheduled Saturday message listing what is still open. Same bridge, same agents and the same medium risk, and the Saturday message is a single job switch that needs nothing beyond wave A pieces.
name: Shared Reminders lists: add, tick off and read by text, plus a Saturday shop list

rationale: F043's handbook already names home systems and providers as its content, and F034 is that section plus a way to fill it from a photo of a data plate; a parent asks the same store either way. Both are ready now at medium risk on the parents' own agents, and F034 depends only on wave A pieces (the vault and photo reading), so no dependency holds it in B.
name: Household knowledge vault: shared family handbook, including the home systems and service-provider registry

rationale: G010 is G009 with an answer coming back: the same family-only pinned send, plus an open-request row and a match on the other parent's yes or no. It depends only on wave A pieces (G009, the household store, reminders) and adds no new recipient or data source, so it is an extension and not a new kind of risk; the card keeps G009's medium risk.
name: Family delivery: pass a message to the other parent or the group, and ask-and-relay with a reply

rationale: AUT-04 and AUT-08 are both written on top of the G003 registry: one states each registered job's authority, the other gives it a time limit, a tool cap, a failure alert to Tony and a missed-run rule. All three are wave A, low risk and operator-only, generated from the same family file, and neither add-on has any use without registered jobs.
name: Jobs registry: per-feature flags, a written charter per job, and unattended-job guardrails

rationale: Both let either parent stop Happy by texting an exact phrase, for everything or for one lost phone, and CRT-02 is specified as an extension of the G005 plugin's hook. Same wave and low risk, and the phrases can only narrow access; the card should say that the lock-out half also falls under decision 15.
name: Stop phrases: 'Happy, stop everything' and lock out one person's handle

rationale: Both are deny entries in the same gateway node-command list, set before any Mac app or phone is paired, and both only tighten. Same wave, low risk, operator-only and no agent gains anything, so it is one config change with two halves.
name: Node command ceiling: deny computer control and phone commands before any device is paired

rationale: Both are host-side, read-only checks that text Tony only when something is wrong, and OCL-13 names G008's delivery path as its own. Same wave and low risk with no tool given to any agent; they differ only in what is checked and how often.
name: Operator self-checks: daily integration health and credential expiry, security audit after updates and monthly

rationale: Both decide when Happy's unprompted texts may arrive: G001 sets the standing limits and G002 lets a parent pause them for a window while urgent alerts still pass. Same wave and low risk, both keep their state in the household store, and no agent or read-versus-write boundary is crossed.
name: Notification policy: quiet hours, daily cap, priority classes, and snooze, mute or vacation mode by chat

rationale: All three are the same isolated per-parent job reading the family calendar and home weather, and differ only in the hour they run and the window they cover. Same wave, agent, tools and medium risk; each stays its own switch in the jobs registry, and the mail digests stay separate cards because other agents hold mail.
name: Family briefs from calendar and weather: evening logistics (19:30), weekday morning (07:00), Sunday week-ahead (18:00)

rationale: F051 is the mailbox and its reader, and F056 and F055 are the two things parents receive from it: routine mail in the afternoon digest and closures or delays at once. Same wave, same school-mail reader, all low risk and all under the mail-path decision, with no parent's private inbox involved.
name: School mailbox: isolated reader, weekday 16:00 digest, and one-line urgent alerts

rationale: Both are one-time, per-platform recipes that make a school system email one predictable summary to the school mailbox, which the digest then turns into a line per child. Same wave and same reader; they stay apart from the mailbox card because these emails carry grades and missing work, and the card keeps SRC-08's medium risk.
name: School platform feeds into the school mailbox: ParentSquare, PowerSchool and Google Classroom guardian summaries

rationale: All three text a parent only when an official recall matches the family's own list, using the same no-model scheduled script with a seen-id file. All are low risk and read-only, and SRC-05 sat in C with no dependency of its own, so the set can ship in B.
name: Recall watch matched to what the family owns: products (CPSC), food and medicine (FDA), vehicles (NHTSA)

rationale: Each is a table of household dates plus a scheduled job that texts a parent ahead of the date and stays silent otherwise, and the tables already overlap (car inspection, health check-ups). All four are wave B, read-only nudges on the parents' own agents with nothing renewed, ordered or paid; the card carries the higher medium risk.
name: Household dates program: upkeep and bins, car and pet care, renewals and expiries, birthdays and gift dates

rationale: CRT-13 names its emergency plan page as the source of the F036 sitter sheet: both turn the same contacts, medical notes and routines into a one-page card for whoever is minding the children. Same wave and the same private agent, Happy sends nothing to anyone outside the family, and the card carries F036's medium risk.
name: Emergency card and sitter sheet from one set of family facts, plus a fixed reply to emergency texts

rationale: CRT-12 uses F067 for its copy-paste answers, so both serve one chore: getting school, camp and sports forms completed from facts Happy already holds while the parent signs and submits. F067 never had a wave, both are medium risk on the parent's own agent, and nothing is filled in or submitted by Happy.
name: Enrolment and camp paperwork kit: document index, due-date reminders and copy-paste form answers

rationale: G015 is the locked-down agent, F047 the read-only Gmail tools it holds and F052 the question a parent asks through them; none of the three is usable without the other two. Same wave, same per-person agent, medium risk and all under decision 1; drafts stay a separate card because they are a write path.
name: Per-person mail agent with read-only Gmail: search, 'did I get an email about X?' and thread summaries

rationale: F053 is the workflow of the F048 drafts tool, so a parent gets one outcome: a threaded draft waiting in their own Gmail to edit and send. Same wave, agent and medium risk; the send block stays in place and the read-only mail card stays separate.
name: Gmail drafts: Happy writes a reply or note into the owner's Drafts, the owner sends

rationale: F060 is built on the F050 watch for clinic, pharmacy and airline senders, and F050 alone gives a parent nothing they would name. F050 never had a wave, both are medium risk with the same tool-less reader, and both concern a parent's private inbox, so the school mailbox decision is not blurred.
name: Trusted-sender watch on a parent's Gmail: appointment, refill, results and travel-change emails become reminders and alerts

rationale: All seven are parts of one future kids agent (its base, what a child can ask it, and how parents oversee it), and each is blocked on the same things: a local model and the children's own accounts, with decision 5 keeping the kids off until then. Nothing here can ship or be decided separately today, so one card carries the whole at medium risk; the parent-run quiz (MKT-02) stays its own wave B card.
name: Kids agent (waits for a local model): own handle, homework hints and drills, weekly card, check-in relay, chat hours, parent alerts and nightly digest

rationale: Decision 11 treats the Hue and Sonos plugins as one option: both live in the same stateless home agent with allowlists and quiet hours in code, HOM-02 records why these two bundled tools were chosen, and F081 reads both to report what is still on. All are wave C; the card states that it switches lights and speakers and carries high risk, and locks, garage, alarm and gate stay excluded.
name: House devices by text: Hue lights and Sonos through the stateless home agent, with a read-only goodnight check

rationale: 'TV off' is F078's own example, and HOM-11's first route is that same Shortcut run by the F078 plugin; its second route (a notice on screen) waits for Home Assistant and is a note, not a separate build. Same wave, both high risk, and the same exact-name allowlist.
name: Allowlisted macOS Shortcuts (goodnight, TV off at bedtime)

rationale: HOM-14 says it adds one thing to F080: the Sunday fridge sheet that F080's own name already includes, made by a script with no model call. Same wave and the same printer queue; the card keeps F080's high risk and states that the weekly sheet involves no agent.
name: Print it: PDFs, photos and pages to the home printer, and the Sunday fridge sheet as a no-model job

rationale: Both answer 'what does the porch look like' with one still picture, and IPH-02 says it extends F079, which is parked because the house has no network camera. Both are 'later' and wait on hardware the house does not have set up; the card states both routes and carries the phone route's high risk.
name: Camera snapshot on request: a network camera (none today) or a spare iPhone on a stand

rationale: Both exist to reach a school or team app that offers no email or website, on the same dedicated Android phone that decision 8 treats as one option. Both are later, experimental and high risk; the card must state the two halves separately, relaying notifications and tapping inside the app.
name: A spare Android phone for app-only school and team apps: relay chosen notifications, and (riskier) operate the app

rationale: Both answer one question, whether Happy can manage a child's device or approve a child's request, with the same no; CRT-07 says it covers what the Screen Time entry leaves out. Both are 'never' records for the same reason (the authority stays with the two adults in the vendors' own apps), so one sourced record is enough.
name: Kids' device controls (Apple Screen Time, Family Link, school Chromebook, console): not through Happy

rationale: Installing and pairing the app is one act that creates both the device node IPH-01 describes and the chat surface OCL-01 describes, under decision 7 and the same Tony-only limit. Same wave; the card must state the node half (device commands) and carries its high risk.
name: OpenClaw iOS app on Tony's iPhone: pairing as node and operator console, native chat with files, approvals and push

rationale: VOX-03 is the set of limits that goes in before any voice surface is switched on and has no use alone, and VOX-05 is one reply style for the same Talk loop. All three fall under the same pairing and voice decisions and add no agent or send path, so they ship with Talk in D at its high risk.
name: Talk mode on Tony's iPhone with the voice guardrails pack (hands-free kitchen session as one use)

rationale: None of the six is worth anything alone: the Mac app node, the clean virtual machine, the desk agent, the human view, the ten-task test and the first form-filling chore are steps of one attended pilot under decision 6. All are 'later' and the card carries high risk; the wave A deny entry (MAC-04) stays a separate card so the default remains off.
name: Screen-control pilot: Mac app on a clean virtual machine, one stateless desk agent, human view, acceptance test, first chore
